Or: then We returned him, after that proportioning and beautifying, to the lowest of the low in beauty of form and shape, when We reversed him in his creation, so that his back bent after being straight, his hair turned white after being black, his skin became wrinkled and his skin, which had been smooth, slackened, and every part of him was changed: his sight and hearing, which had been sharp, dulled, his walk became slow and gentle ["dalif," meaning a slow walk with close steps], his voice became faint, his strength became weakness, and his dignity became ["kharaf," senility; the text reads "khawf"]. 

And 'Abdullah [ibn Mas'ud] read: "asfala al-safilin" (the lowest of the low).

If you ask: how is the exception (in ﴿except those who believe﴾) according to the two views? I say: according to the first, it is connected and clearly so; according to the second, it is disconnected. That is: but those who were righteous among the aged have an everlasting reward that does not end, for their obedience and their patience over God's trial with old age and decrepitude, and for enduring hardships and standing in worship despite their weakened rising.

If you ask: who is the addressee of ﴿So what makes you deny the Judgment?﴾? I say: it is addressed to man by way of iltifat (a shift in grammatical person), meaning: what makes you a liar, because of religion and denying it after this proof? That is, you are lying when you deny the recompense, because every one who denies the truth is a liar. So what compels you to be a liar by denying recompense? The "ba'" here is like its use in God's words: ﴿Those who take him as a friend, and those who associate others with him﴾ [12:106]. The meaning is: that the creation of man from a drop of semen, his shaping as a perfect human being, his gradual progression through stages of growth until he matures and becomes complete, and then his reversal until he reaches the lowest age: you will not see any clearer proof than this of the power of the Creator, and that whoever has power over all this is not incapable of bringing him back. So what is the cause of your denial, O man, of the recompense after this decisive proof?

It has also been said that the address is to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). ﴿Is not God the most just of judges?﴾ is a threat to the disbelievers, that He will judge them by what they deserve.

It is reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that when he recited it, he would say: "Yes, and I am among the witnesses to that." Meccan, and its verses are 8 [revealed after Surat al-Buruj]. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

He swears by them (the fig and the olive) because they are remarkable among the kinds of fruit-bearing trees. It is reported that a tray of figs was presented as a gift to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He ate from it and said to his companions: "Eat. If I said that a fruit had come down from Paradise, I would say it was this one, because the fruit of Paradise has no pits, so eat it. For it cuts off hemorrhoids and benefits gout." [Narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Tibb; al-Tha'labi from the hadith of Abu Dhar. Among its narrators is one who is not known.] Mu'adh ibn Jabal passed by an olive tree, took a twig from it, and used it as a toothstick, and said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'The olive is an excellent siwak (toothstick), from the blessed tree; it sweetens the mouth and removes the phlegm.'" And I heard him say: "It is my siwak and the siwak of the prophets before me." [Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and al-Tha'labi from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal; its isnad is weak.]

From Ibn 'Abbas (may God be pleased with him): "It is your fig and your olive." It has also been said: they are two mountains of the Holy Land, called in Syriac Tur Tina and Tur Zita, because they are the places where the fig and the olive grow. It has been said that "the fig" refers to the mountains between Hulwan and Hamadan, and "the olive" refers to the mountains of Syria, because these are where they grow, as if it were said: "and the places where the fig and the olive grow."

"Tur" (the mountain) is made idafa (construct phrase) with "Sinin," which is the place. Regarding "Sinin," there is "Sinun" and "Yabrun": in permitting the declension with waw and ya, in retaining the ya, and in moving the nun with the vowels of declension (i'rab, grammatical case endings).

"Al-balad" is Mecca, may God protect it. "Al-Amin" (the trustworthy) is from "amina al-rajul amanatan, fa-huwa amin" (the man was trustworthy). It has been said that it is "aman," as it is said "kiram" for "karim" (noble). Its trustworthiness is that it protects whoever enters it, as the trustworthy man protects what is entrusted to him. It is also permissible that it be fa'il in the sense of maf'ul, from "amanahu," because he is safe from harm, just as it is described as safe in God's words: ﴿a sanctuary secure﴾, meaning: possessing security. The meaning of the oath by these things is as follows.

The purpose is to declare the nobility of these blessed places and the good and blessing that appeared in them through the dwelling of the prophets and the righteous. The place where the fig and the olive grow is the migration site of Abraham, and the birthplace and upbringing of Jesus. "Al-Tur" is the place from which Moses was called. Mecca is the place of the House, which is ﴿guidance for the worlds﴾, and the birthplace and mission of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).
